_internal: `subsistence_from_climate` names the floor per person sim/world/climate_needs.py calculates for each tile from its climate. TRANSITIONAL: surplus_budget_share is a labelled heuristic weight per need (water's is small because its floor is most of what a household spends on it) (normalised over the needs that have a priced good). A good's effectiveness is per unit of its own production unit, in the need's unit. Mods add needs (ids namespaced by mod id) and add or extend goods; a production entry may also carry `satisfies` for its dominant output.

food.effectiveness_basis: food energy per kg relative to wheat grain
food.satiation_basis: BIOLOGICAL limit, not a heuristic: well-fed modern intake, about 3,300 kcal per person per day (FAO food balance sheets: dietary energy supply in 2021 was about 3,460 kcal a head a day in Europe and 3,880 in Northern America, FAO food balance sheets update, https://www.fao.org/3/cc8088en/cc8088en.pdf; supply includes household waste, so intake is lower), over the 3,400 kcal per kg of wheat the subsistence figure uses, a year of it: 1.5 times the subsistence quantity. Food beyond it is stored, sold, fed to animals or wasted. Held equal to sim/world/agriculture.py MAXIMUM_INTAKE_MULTIPLE_OF_SUBSISTENCE by a test.

shelter.satiation_basis: Past a roomy dwelling, more wall and roof is not wanted, and a household that has money left builds no more house with it. The floor is the Sphere minimum covered area of 3.5 square metres a head; living space in pre-industrial housing was of the order of ten square metres a head, about three times that (floor areas of peasant and urban tenement dwellings, recalled and not re-opened; confidence D). The limit is that multiple of the tile's own floor, since the floor follows the climate's wall thickness.
shelter.unit: cubic metres of wall or frame
shelter.effectiveness_basis: volume of structure one unit builds

clothing.effectiveness_basis: cover and warmth per kg relative to plain woven cloth

implements_and_arms.effectiveness_basis: working hardness and edge holding per kg relative to bronze

health.effectiveness_basis: relative therapeutic or hygienic effect per kg

ornament.unit: kg of bright durable metal equivalent
ornament.satiation_basis: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: ornament metal is durable, so yearly purchase is wear and loss of the stock held, not the budget share; about 25 g held per head and about 2 per cent worn or lost a year. Validation bound used by tests: at most a few grams per head per year. A held-stock model would replace it.
ornament.effectiveness_basis: display value per kg of worked metal; a cultural quantity, equal across the bright metals

seasoning.satiation_basis: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: spices are bought for taste and to dress plain food, and a household's yearly use is grams, not a budget share; a couple of grams per head a year is an order of magnitude, not a measured figure. A model of taste, and of how far an elite's use exceeds the common people's, would replace it.
seasoning.effectiveness_basis: flavouring strength per kg relative to black pepper; taken equal across the spices until a source gives them separately

salt.subsistence_basis: BIOLOGICAL requirement: the Institute of Medicine Adequate Intake for adult sodium is 1.5 g a day (Dietary Reference Intakes for Water, Potassium, Sodium, Chloride, and Sulfate, National Academies Press, 2005), set to cover sodium lost in sweat by people active in heat. Sodium is 39.3 per cent of sodium chloride by mass (22.99 / 58.44), so 1.5 g of sodium is 3.81 g of salt a day, 3.81 * 365 = 1.39 kg a year. Bare survival needs far less on a cool, idle day; this is the floor for working people in a warm climate. The source was recalled, not re-opened; confidence C.
salt.satiation_basis: BIOLOGICAL limit: typical modern adult intake is about 10 g of salt a day (World Health Organization, Guideline: Sodium intake for adults and children, 2012, reports mean intakes of 9 to 12 g a day in most countries), 10 * 365 = 3.65 kg a year, past which the extra only harms. The source was recalled, not re-opened; confidence C.
salt.effectiveness_basis: mass of sodium chloride; rock, solar and brine salt are equal

water.subsistence_basis: 20 litres a head a day, the basic-access service level of Howard and Bartram, Domestic Water Quantity, Service Level and Health (WHO, 2003): enough for drinking, cooking and basic hygiene; survival drinking alone is a few litres. One litre is one kilogram, so 20 * 365 = 7300 kg. The source was recalled, not re-opened; confidence C.
water.satiation_basis: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: 100 litres a head a day, the 'optimal access' level of the same WHO report, past which more water is waste, not use. Roman fountains ran at far higher flows; that is a flow, not a use per head.
water.unit: kg of water at the point of use
water.effectiveness_basis: mass of water delivered; every way of delivering it is equal

vessels.stock_basis: A household holds a few dozen vessels (cooking pots, storage jars, bowls, cups) of about a kilogram each, about 5 kg a head, and they break and are replaced within a few years: cooking pots last the least, storage jars the most. Ethnoarchaeological studies of household pottery (Deal, Household Pottery Disposal in the Maya Highlands, 1998, recalled and not re-opened) give the order of the stock and its use-life; confidence D. The floor is the stock over its life, as for any durable.
vessels.effectiveness_basis: mass of ware; fired clay and glass are taken equal until a source gives their use-lives separately

writing.floor_basis: No floor: nobody dies or goes cold for want of writing, and a floor is bought whatever it costs, which would put writing into the wage a household must earn. Households spend a share of their surplus on it, and the share applies to the literate part of the population, which is the civilisation's literacy_general, so it grows as schooling spreads.
writing.effectiveness_basis: one written page of a letter or document

money.stock_basis: Silver coin in circulation in a large pre-industrial money economy is of the order of a tenth of a kilogram a head, and wear, loss and hoarding take about one and a half per cent of it a year (Duncan-Jones, Money and Government in the Roman Empire, 1994, recalled and not re-opened; confidence D). The mint's own striking and wear are modelled in sim/economy/mint.py; this entry is only so the labour package sees the engravers and furnacemen that coin replacement keeps at work, and households do not buy it.

light.floor_basis: No floor: nobody dies for want of light after dark, and a floor is bought whatever it costs. Households spend a share of their surplus on it. A tallow candle gives about one candela, about 12.6 lumens, so a thousand lumen-hours is about eighty candle-hours (recalled, not re-opened; confidence D).
light.satiation_basis: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: about four lit evening hours a day at a few hundred lumens a household's room, shared among its people, is the order of what a household lights in a year before more light is waste; not a measured figure. A model of the hours people stay up and the rooms they light would replace it.
light.effectiveness_basis: light given per unit of the good, in thousands of lumen-hours

amusement.floor_basis: No floor: nobody dies for want of a game. Households spend a share of their surplus on it, where a table or a lottery is open to them.
amusement.satiation_basis: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: about four hours of play a week for each person, past which a household's spending on stakes and tables turns to other things; not a measured figure. A model of leisure time would replace it.
amusement.effectiveness_basis: one hour of play at a table, or one numbered chance, taken as equal

fat_kg.basis: Not a food here: rendered tallow from sheep and cattle served lighting and soap, and the edible animal fat of the period was lard from pigs, which are not modelled (Complaints/532). A good that does serve a need may declare max_share_of_need, the largest share of that need's units it can meet.

bread_kg.basis: Calories of the flour in a kilogram of loaf: the flour factor times the flour in a kilogram of bread (data/production/95_bread.json); water and baking add no food energy.

fish_kg.basis: Edible fish at 900 kcal a kilogram over wheat grain's 3400 (WHEAT_ENERGY_KCAL_PER_KG); the same energy as the fisher's hours return (data/production/95_fish.json), counted once as the good.

salted_fish_kg.basis: The fresh fish's energy in 700 kg of cured fish from 1000 kg: 0.265 * 1000 / 700; curing adds and loses no energy (data/production/95_fish.json).

garum_kg.basis: A condiment: no food energy is counted, and no need ranks fish sauce among the seasonings yet (seasoning is in pepper equivalents). Bought as an input and traded as a good.

light.basis: Quality against beeswax, the clean-burning reference (factor one): tallow smokes, smells of burnt fat, gutters and sags in summer heat, so a household that can afford wax pays more per unit of light for it. The factor is a household's valuation, not light delivered (lumen-hours stay in effectiveness). Beeswax against tallow is recalled from histories of domestic lighting (smokeless, brighter, sweet-smelling, several times dearer); the number is a placeholder, not a measurement.
light.retire: indoor air model (smoke and ventilation), Complaint 565 follow-up
